questions.q: The bond length of the species \[{O_2},O_2^ + \] and \[O_2^ - \] are in the order of:-
questions.s:
As we know \[bond\,order\, \propto \,\frac{1}{{bond\,length}}\]
\[\begin{gathered}
 O_2^ + \, = \,2.5 \\
 {O_2}\, = \,2 \\
 O_2^ - \, = \,1.5 \\ 
\end{gathered} \]
Therefore bond length order is \[O_2^ - > {O_2} > O_2^ + \]

questions.q: The dipole moment of o, p and m-dichlorobenzene will be in the order
questions.s:
[IMAGE NOT CAPTURED] μ = 0 μ = \[\sqrt 3 \]x μ = x
In p-dichlorobenzene, two C-Cl dipoles cancel each other
∴ μ = 0.
In o-dichlorobenzene, the two C-Cl dipoles (say x) are inclined at an angle of 60°. Therefore, according to parallelogram law of forces, the resultant
\[\begin{gathered}
 = \sqrt {{x^2} + {x^2} + 2{x^2} \times \cos {{60}^{\text{o}}}} \\
 = \sqrt {{x^2} + {x^2} + 2{x^2} \times 1/2} = \sqrt {3{x^2}} = \sqrt {3}x \\ 
\end{gathered} \]
In m-dichlorobenzene, the two dipoles are inclined to each other at an angle of 120°, therefore, resultant
\[\begin{gathered}
 = \sqrt {{x^2} + {x^2} + 2{x^2} \times \cos {{120}^{\text{o}}}} \\
 = \sqrt {{x^2} + {x^2} + 2{x^2} \times \left( { - 1/2} \right)} = \sqrt {{x^2}} = x \\ 
\end{gathered} \]
Thus, the decreasing order of dipole moments is o > m > p .
